factors-multiples.why: Factors divide into a number; multiples are built from it. A number has finitely many factors and endlessly many multiples. Keeping the two words straight is most of the battle.
traps: To list factors you only need to test up to the square root — past that the pairs repeat.

divisibility-rules.why: Divisibility rules let you factor by inspection instead of by trial division, and they all come from place value. The rule for 3 works because 10 leaves remainder 1 when divided by 3, so only the digit sum matters.
traps: Divisible by 2 and by 3 means divisible by 6 — but divisible by 2 and by 4 does not mean divisible by 8. The shortcut only works when the factors share nothing.

primes-composites.why: Primes are the atoms of multiplication: every whole number is a product of them, in exactly one way. That uniqueness is what makes GCF, LCM, fraction simplification and modern cryptography work.
traps: 1 is not prime. It has only one factor, and admitting it would destroy the uniqueness of prime factorisation.

prime-factorisation.why: Factorising into primes is like getting a number's fingerprint. Once you have it, the greatest common factor, the least common multiple, whether a fraction will terminate, and whether a root simplifies all become readable at a glance.
traps: Keep dividing until every factor is prime. Stopping at 4 × 9 is not a prime factorisation.

gcf.why: The greatest common factor is what two numbers share. It is the thing you cancel to put a fraction in lowest terms and the thing you factor out of an algebraic expression — the same operation in two costumes.
traps: Use the GCF, not just any common factor, or you will have to simplify twice.

code.note: The Euclidean algorithm behind this is 2,300 years old and still the fastest known method.

lcm.why: The least common multiple is the first moment two cycles line up — two buses leaving together, two gears meeting, two fractions sharing a denominator. GCF is about splitting things up; LCM is about things coinciding.
traps: Word problems about events repeating together want the LCM. Problems about splitting into equal groups want the GCF. Ask which one the situation is.
